structure: Part 3, address book add, edit and journey handshake, read in full from repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend: features/address-book/add/ (add.controller.js 152 lines, add.njk 118), edit/ (edit.controller.js 138, edit.njk 111), fields.js (field rules and the Joi rule set), address-countries.js (country list for the select, GB pinned first), handshake-context.js and journey-registry.js (the journey handshake with the animals frontend), copy/copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (add, edit, form, errors and success-banner keys claimed; list, view and delete keys left to part 2), lib/validate/ (index.js, run.js, validators.js, calendar.js: the shared Joi validators), services/countries/ (client.js, index.js, stub.js: reference-data countries with a process-wide cache and a four-country stub) and services/address-book/client.js (create and update calls with organisation scoping), plus the fit specs add.fit.spec.js (19 tests once the required and max-length loops expand) and edit.fit.spec.js (7 tests) with their helpers address-form.js and axe.js. To ground what the read files call, I also looked at shared/kit.js (error summary, page title, organisation check), shared/paths.js, services/address-book/index.js (API error mapping), features/address-book/address-id-params.js, stored-address.js, success-banner.js, common/constants/journey-set-bases.js and common/helpers/set-base-url.js. Covered: the add page at /address-book/add (heading, two section headings, nine fields with labels, hint, autocomplete, widths and required/optional, country options and their source, save and cancel, Cache-Control), the edit page at /address-book/{id}/edit (id check, prefill, back link, save, cancel, not-found and deleted handling), every validation rule and its English and Welsh message, how the error summary links to fields and values are preserved, server-side validation and failure states, the create and update payloads and organisation scoping, the success banners, the handshake (one registered journey type gbn-ag to the animals frontend's live-animals set, four query parameters, all-or-none rule, session storage, hidden fields, the cancel label, the return URL with handshake-token and addressId), the shared validators and calendar helpers the address form does and does not use, and every test in both fit specs. Gaps recorded where the slice is silent: no caption, no handshake on edit, no fit test of the handshake, no postcode or phone format rule, no verification of the handshake token.

claims.statement: Saving a new address sends a POST to the address book service at /organisation/{organisation id}/addresses.

The create and update requests send a JSON body of exactly the nine form fields: name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone and email, with blank optional fields sent as empty strings.
claims.note: Inferred: the controller builds formValues from FIELDS only, validates them and sends the validated value as the body.

claims.statement: Every address book request carries the signed-in user's organisation id both in the path and in a 'Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id' header, so addresses are scoped to the user's organisation.
claims.quote: // The organisation header is the authorisation — the address book trusts it with no further authentication (see its IdentityHeaderFilter). It must come only from the authenticated session, and must match the orgId in the path (cv-010).

claims.statement: Security: the address book service relies on the organisation identity the frontend passes it, with no further authentication of its own, so the frontend's session is the only guard on organisation scoping.
claims.quote: the address book trusts it with no further authentication
claims.note: Recorded in general terms only.

The edit page does not support the journey handshake: it has no journey hidden fields and always returns to the address book.
claims.note: Looked in edit.controller.js and edit.njk: neither reads or carries handshake context. Whether a journey user should be able to edit an address and return is not stated.

claims.statement: One journey is registered for the handshake: journey type 'gbn-ag'.
The 'gbn-ag' journey returns to the animals frontend, at its configured base URL plus the '/live-animals' journey set base.
The return path into the journey is /notifications/{notification-id}/address-return?fulfilment-id={fulfilment-id}, with both ids URL-encoded.
A journey sends the user to the add page with four query parameters: journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token.
claims.quote:
journeyType: queryValue(request, 'journey-type'),
    notificationId: queryValue(request, 'notification-id'),
    fulfilmentId: queryValue(request, 'fulfilment-id'),
    handshakeToken: queryValue(request, 'handshake-token')

claims.statement: Handshake parameter values are trimmed, and a blank value counts as absent.
The handshake parameters must be sent all together or not at all: some but not all of them gives a 400 'Incomplete journey handshake' error.
A handshake with a journey type that is not registered shows the page not found error.

The return URL is never taken from the request: it is built on the server from the registered journey's configured base URL and path template, so a journey cannot send the user back to an arbitrary address.
claims.note: Inferred: the only check on the return destination is that the journey type is in the registry; the ids are encoded into a fixed template.

claims.statement: The address book does not verify the handshake token, notification id or fulfilment id; it only carries them and passes them back to the journey.
claims.note: Inferred: no code in the slice checks the token's value; verifying it is presumably the journey frontend's job on return.

claims.statement: Opening the add page with a valid handshake stores the journey context in the user's session; opening it with no handshake parameters clears any stored journey context.
In journey mode the add form carries the journey context as hidden fields (journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id, handshake-token) so it survives the submit.

On submit, journey context in the form takes precedence and is re-stored in the session; if the form carries none, the context stored in the session is used, and a stored context with an unregistered journey type is discarded.
In journey mode the add page keeps the same heading, fields and 'Save and continue' button; the only visible difference is the cancel button, which reads 'Cancel and return to address page'.
claims.quote: cancelToJourney: 'Cancel and return to address page'

claims.statement: Saving a new address in journey mode sends the user back to the journey's return URL with the handshake-token and the new address's id as 'addressId' added to the query.
Saving in journey mode shows no success banner in the address book.
Cancelling the add page in journey mode sends the user back to the journey's return URL with the handshake-token but no addressId.
In journey mode, validation errors and save failures re-show the add form still in journey mode.
Only the animals frontend's live-animals journey is registered; there is no handshake entry for the plants journey or any other journey.
claims.note: Looked in journey-registry.js and journey-set-bases.js: only gbn-ag and live-animals exist.
